catlasr

R infrastructure for the CATLAS project: the code engine that imports, validates and scores the data of the CATLAS experiments, while CATLAS itself contains the manuscripts and analysis notebooks. The experiments run on code documented in catlaslab.

Status

v0.0.1 is a pre-release, tagged before data collection of fba-allergy-online-02, the pre-registered replication of three-stage forward blocking (Beesley & Le Pelley, 2011). Its pre-registration refers to the import, validation, exclusion and scoring functions by name, so from this tag on they are frozen and any later change that could alter a reported number is a deviation from the registered analysis and is logged as such in NEWS.md.

The pre-release contains no data. The anonymised data of fba-allergy-online-02 will be added in a later release.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("josefmana/catlasr@v0.0.1")

# Only needed to download data from JATOS
remotes::install_github("visionlabels/jatosR")

What it does

Every analysis step is a function called deliberately by the user and every function states its assumptions as it runs.

  • Import from JATOS
    pull_jatos_batches() downloads study results, reading the complete jsPsych data from the result file when the experiment uploaded one and from the streamed data otherwise; parse_jatos_results() and repair_jatos_json() turn JATOS imports into trial tables.
  • Data bundles
    build_provenance() records where the data come from, build_fba_rawdata() builds and validate_fba_rawdata() validates a forward-blocking data bundle (participant metadata, stimulus mappings and trials), and record_exclusion() removes participants while recording the exclusion rule in the bundle’s provenance.
  • Learning check
    score_learning(), test_learning(), screen_learning(), aggregate_learning() and plot_learning() run in a series.
  • Blocking indices
    score_blocking(), index_blocking() (the confidence-weighted choice score of Beesley & Le Pelley, 2011, and the choice-proportion score of Paskewitz & Jones, 2020), aggregate_blocking() and plot_blocking(), run in a series.
  • Data collection monitoring
    trace_progress() reports how far every participant got without reading any test response.
  • Stimuli
    catlas_stimulus(), render_stimulus() and write_stimulus() compose the cue and outcome images of the allergist task.

Personal data

Personal data never enter any repository. They live in a private folder outside every git repository, named by the environment variable CATLAS_PRIVATE_DIR in .Renviron, with one subfolder per study.

  • write_private_rds(), write_private_csv() and read_private_rds() ensure privacy by refusing any folder inside a git work tree.
  • update_id_key() replaces platform identifiers by random participant IDs, keeping the key in the private folder only.
  • Data bundles refuse e-mail addresses and free-text answers. The free-text debriefing answers are coded manually blind to the test data, with write_debrief_coding() and read_debrief_coding().

  • Importing the Forward Blocking Replication Pilot from JATOS: the import of the pilot fba-allergy-online-01, step by step.
  • Generating Stimuli for the Allergist Task: the image generation code for fba-allergy-online-01 and fba-allergy-online-02 study materials.

Paskewitz, S., & Jones, M. (2020). Dissecting EXIT. Journal of Mathematical Psychology, 97, 102371. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmp.2020.102371
